clue.text: Seat in parliament once

definitions.meaning: the seat is the backside, the hindquarters one sits on
the Long Parliament's remnant after Pride's Purge of 1648 was known by this name

explanation.surface: Someone recalls holding a seat in the Commons in years gone by.
explanation.definitionFit: The buttocks are what one sits on, and the purged Long Parliament of 1648-53 bore the same name as a historical nickname.

clue.text: Revolutionary spoke around clubs

indicators.note: around says the spoke word goes round the clubs abbreviation

parts.note: a spoke is a radial, as in a wheel
C is the card-game abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A wheel spoke turns round some clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoke' looks like a verb, but it is the noun for a wheel's rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A militant reformer seeking sweeping change, as an adjective, is extreme.

clue.text: One's in the sea off Calais man, that's close

indicators.note: in puts the I-is pair inside the French sea word

parts.note: mer is French for sea, as spoken in Calais
One's is I plus is, giving IS

explanation.surface: Someone is in the water off the French coast, near enough to touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' means stingy here, not near.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight-fisted, close person hoards money, so he is mean with it.

clue.text: Medic's warning finally accepted on sulphur pollution

indicators.note: accepted on means the following pieces are taken on after the symbol for sulphur

parts.note: S is the chemical symbol for sulphur
MO, medical officer, is a common crossword medic

indicators.note: finally asks for only the closing letter of the word warning

explanation.surface: A doctor's caution about sulphur in the air has at last been heeded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes G from 'warning'; 'accepted on' puts MO and G after S.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a blend of smoke and fog, a type of urban air pollution.

clue.text: Byron's end covered in gloomy elegy

indicators.note: covered in says the letter is wrapped inside the word for gloomy

parts.note: moody means gloomy

indicators.note: end asks for the final letter of the poet's name

explanation.surface: Byron's death is marked in a melancholy lament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end' takes N from 'Byron's', and 'covered in' puts it inside MOODY.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a mournful poem or song for one voice, a lament.

clue.text: Like a drive? Seriously, inexperienced driver can hop in

indicators.note: can hop in says the learner jumps inside the word for seriously

parts.note: gravely means seriously
L is the learner plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: Fancy a drive? A learner really can get in the car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drive' sounds like motoring but means a driveway, often surfaced with small stones.
explanation.definitionFit: A driveway covered in small stones is pebbly, so the adjective describes it.

clue.text: On horse, desire free ride

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H
an itch is a restless desire

explanation.surface: Sitting on a horse, someone longs for a lift at no cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' just places H at the front of the across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To thumb a lift from passing traffic is to get a free ride, a colloquial sense.

clue.text: What may cause bubble to burst is economic disaster

definitions.text: What may cause bubble to burst
definitions.meaning: blowing a bubble far too full makes it pop
runaway rise in prices is an economic catastrophe

explanation.surface: A financial bubble bursting spells catastrophe for the economy.
explanation.definitionFit: Overblowing a bubble pops it, and runaway price rises destroy a currency's value.

clue.text: Islander getting wet in a sea that's stormy

indicators.note: a stormy sea is churned up, so the letters are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: A sailor from an island gets soaked in rough seas.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Taiwan is an inhabitant of that island.

clue.text: Deck opening on extremely elegant cutter

parts.note: a hatch is an opening in a ship's deck

indicators.note: extremely asks for the letters at the extremes of the word elegant

explanation.surface: A ship's hatch leads to a very smart boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutter' suggests a small boat, fitting the deck picture, but it means a chopping tool; 'extremely' gives E and T.
explanation.definitionFit: A small axe is a tool for chopping.

clue.text: One impeached gets justice in US battle

parts.note: Earl Warren was Chief Justice of the US Supreme Court
the Battle of Hastings was fought in 1066

explanation.surface: An impeached official is tried in an American conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: The governor-general of India was impeached in 1787 and acquitted after a seven-year trial.
explanation.definitionFit: The first Governor-General of Bengal was famously impeached by Parliament.

clue.text: International standard wrongly said to be held in contempt

indicators.note: to be held in says the jumbled word sits inside the standard's letters

parts.note: DIN is the German standards body whose norms (paper sizes, plugs) are used internationally

indicators.note: wrongly says the letters of said are set out in a mistaken order

explanation.surface: Someone claims a global standard was falsely described as scorned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held in contempt' looks like one phrase; only 'contempt' is the definition, and 'to be held in' is the container signal. DIN is the German standard adopted worldwide, for example in A4 paper sizes.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorn and contempt are synonyms for the feeling that something is beneath one.

clue.text: Establish a quantity' of liquid has been taken out of river

indicators.note: a measure drawn out of a river has some river within it, so the river's name goes inside

parts.note: a pint is a measure of liquid
the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: Someone sets up the fact that a measure of water was drawn from a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has been taken out of' signals containment by a picture: a measure drawn from a river holds some of that river inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To set up or install someone in a post is to name them to it; establish and nominate overlap here.

clue.text: Sort of paper for which a stunning charge may be made

definitions.meaning: a thick, good-quality drawing paper carries this name

definitions.text: for which a stunning charge may be made
definitions.meaning: a gun or stun-gun ... is made to hold a charge that stuns

explanation.surface: An art paper for which someone asks an astonishing price.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy drawing paper and the explosive-filled case loaded into a gun share the name.

clue.text: Swimmer has nothing to replace energy lost in stretch of river

indicators.note: to replace says the zero takes the place of another letter in the river word
lost in says the energy symbol drops out of the river word

parts.note: a reach is a straight stretch of river between bends
E is the physics symbol for energy
O, the round zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A tired swimmer has run out of energy along part of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater fish, and in crosswords any fish is a swimmer.

clue.text: Pooter, given drug, is like a wild animal

parts.note: Lupin is the son of Charles Pooter in The Diary of a Nobody
E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: Mr Pooter, once drugged, behaves like a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: The Diary of a Nobody is a Victorian comic novel; Lupin is its narrator's son, who shares the Pooter name.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means wolfish, and the wolf is the wild animal intended.

clue.text: Mansfield Park without its heroine would be very funny

parts.note: Fanny Price is the heroine of Jane Austen's Mansfield Park
without means lacking, the sense of the suffix less

explanation.surface: Removing Austen's heroine from her novel would be hilarious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mansfield Park' sets up whose heroine is meant; a novel without Price is literally Price-less.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquially, something hilarious or invaluable is beyond price.

clue.text: Sad to hear dope is among what is incriminatingly concealed

indicators.note: is among puts the information inside the word for framed evidence

parts.note: a plant is evidence hidden to frame someone
dope means information, as does gen

explanation.surface: It is upsetting to hear drugs were found among items planted to incriminate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' looks like drugs, fitting the planting picture, but here it means information.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes a loud, mournful sound, so it is sad when heard.

clue.text: A pair of opponents trap Cold Warrior of old

indicators.note: trap says the letters for A and the opponents enclose the cold word

parts.note: in bridge East and South are opponents, E and S
chill means cold

explanation.surface: Two adversaries ensnare a Cold War fighter of yesteryear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold Warrior' reads as one phrase but splits: 'Cold' is CHILL, 'Warrior' starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek hero of the Trojan War was a warrior of ancient times.

clue.text: Boss in limited company

parts.note: a business-style reading hides the political one: a ruler in a regime run by a small few

explanation.surface: The head of a firm with limited liability.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a ruler belongs to a small clique that holds power, a government of the few.

clue.text: Weird fate of bishop's crook

indicators.note: crook as an adjective means bent or awry, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Strange is the fate of a bishop's crozier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crook' looks like the bishop's staff but means bent, the anagram signal for FATE OF and B.
explanation.definitionFit: Unconventional and odd are synonyms for eccentric.

clue.text: Speaking easily after illness is laryngologist's department

indicators.note: after places the hospital department following the illness

parts.note: flu is a common illness
ENT, ear, nose and throat, is where a throat specialist works

explanation.surface: Someone talks freely after an illness, thanks to the throat clinic.
explanation.definitionFit: Being articulate means talking smoothly and without hesitation.

clue.text: Judge adopted by Labour is in clover

indicators.note: adopted by says the judge is taken inside the labour word

parts.note: toil means hard labour
a ref, referee, judges a game

explanation.surface: A judge welcomed by the Labour Party is living in luxury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the political party; 'in clover', meaning in luxury, hides the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-leaved plant, so a type of clover.

clue.text: Reflective, or vacant sort of look?

definitions.meaning: reflective means shiny like a mirror
an expressionless stare is described this way

explanation.surface: Is that look thoughtful or just blank?
explanation.definitionFit: A mirror-smooth surface reflects light, and a blank, expressionless stare is described the same way.

clue.text: Quick to divide line into groups of syllables

indicators.note: into says the line abbreviation is put inside the metrical units

parts.note: metrical feet are groups of syllables in verse

explanation.surface: A fast way to break a line of verse into metrical units.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a poetry lesson; 'to divide' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift of foot is the sense: rapid, nimble.

clue.text: Nervous as I see a tall stranger

indicators.note: stranger read as more strange signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: I get jittery when I spot a tall stranger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stranger' looks like a noun but is the comparative adjective, signalling that I SEE A TALL is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Being uncomfortable or uneasy is a synonym for being jittery.

clue.text: No bet on whole collection, just this leader

indicators.note: No says the gambling word is removed from the longer word

parts.note: the whole collection of letters from A to Z
bet as written

explanation.surface: Not wagering on the whole set, just the favourite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bet' looks like gambling but is simply removed from the word for the whole set of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The first letter of the Greek letters heads them, hence the dominant one.

clue.text: Never failing to spot seabird in each lake

indicators.note: in puts the seabird inside the abbreviation for each

parts.note: a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: Someone always manages to see a seabird on every lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Everlasting and never-ending are synonyms for something that never fails.

clue.text: Roman general brings men in to replace one star group

indicators.note: brings says the general's name takes on the soldiers' abbreviation
in to replace says the soldiers go in where the numeral one stood

parts.note: Scipio Africanus was the Roman general who defeated Hannibal
I is the Roman numeral one
OR, other ranks, means men as opposed to officers

explanation.surface: A Roman commander brings in troops to replace a solitary star cluster.
explanation.walkthrough: Of the two I's in SCIPIO, the first is replaced by OR.
explanation.definitionFit: A zodiac sign is also a constellation, a group of stars.

clue.text: Applies on time for various jobs

indicators.note: on means the request word follows after the time abbreviation

parts.note: applies for means asks for

explanation.surface: Someone applies punctually for a range of jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Assignments or chores are pieces of work to be done.

clue.text: Broadcaster heard in island

indicators.note: heard says the broadcaster's name is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Sky is a British satellite broadcaster

explanation.surface: A TV channel can be picked up on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: SKYE is a Scottish island in the Inner Hebrides.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the Inner Hebrides, an island off Scotland's west coast.

clue.text: Proceeds to pull

definitions.meaning: proceeds as a noun means takings or loot
to pull means to drag or tow

explanation.definitionFit: A robber's takings are a noun sense, and dragging something heavy is the verb sense.
